sections.overview: The chestnut-bellied sandgrouse is a ground-dwelling bird of dry regions across Africa and southern Asia.
sections.identification: Males show a black breast band and chestnut belly; females are more heavily barred and spotted.
sections.habitat: It inhabits deserts, thorn scrub and other open dry country; in Saudi Arabia it is reported from arid sandy or gravel plains with shrubs.
sections.diet: It feeds mostly on dry seeds.
sections.behavior: It gathers at watering sites, sometimes in large flocks; breeding males can carry water to chicks in specialized breast feathers.
sections.reproduction: It nests in a simple scrape on bare ground; the usual clutch has three eggs, and both sexes incubate.
sections.ecology: Its dry-seed diet makes dependable access to water important in arid landscapes.
sections.conservation: BirdLife’s IUCN assessment lists it as Least Concern, citing its very large range and apparently stable population.
